subject: Quantum Retail POC — post-call recap, integration plan & next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@quantumretail.com>, Lena Torres <lena.t@quantumretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:05:00-04:00
Subject: Quantum Retail — POC recap & immediate next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — nice to meet the Quantum team. Quick recap and proposed POC approach so we can align on scope and timeline. Please reply with any corrections.

High-level POC objective:
- Validate Redwood’s streaming + tool-calling flow for real-time product recommendations inside Quantum’s customer UI, within existing infra constraints.

Agreed success criteria (draft) — attached as PDF:
- Recommendation latency: median < 250ms under 95th percentile load (production-like traffic sample)
- Relevance: top-3 CTR >= 35% on seeded test set (Quantum provides test set)
- Cost target: < $0.015 per thousand tokens served on average for the POC workload
- Security: mutual-TLS + audit logs available to Quantum for the duration of the trial

POC plan (6 weeks, tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): confirm success criteria and infra constraints, sign MSA SOW addendum
- Week 1: dev kickoff — Redwood provides SDK snippets + sample streaming integration
- Weeks 2–4: integration & data run (prefix caching enabled, nightly evaluation runs)
- Week 5: joint acceptance run and evaluation
- Week 6: retro + decision / rollout planning

Ownership:
- Redwood technical lead / dev owner: Ben Carter (ben@redwood.com) — will own SDK/route handoff and sample code
- Redwood solutions lead: me (Aisha) — PM for the POC and commercial touchpoints
- Quantum tech owner: Samir (cc’d) — please confirm any additional Quantum stakeholders

Integration notes / asks for the call:
- Can you confirm whether Quantum will accept a client-initiated streaming connection (server-sent tokens) or prefers short-polling?
- Any gateway constraints (mutual-TLS, client cert management, IP allowlists)?
- Who will provide the evaluation test set and is there a preferred S3/secure transfer location?

Attachments: quantum_poc_success_criteria.pdf, redwood_integration_checklist.xlsx

Next step: Samir / Lena — confirm infra constraints and acceptance criteria; Ben and I will draft a 1-page technical kickoff and proposed workplan once we have those answers.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[aisha@redwood.com]

[Attachment: quantum_poc_success_criteria.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: redwood_integration_checklist.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Samir Patel <samir@quantumretail.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quantum Retail — POC recap & immediate next steps

Aisha — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side and a couple of constraints: 

1) Ownership: I'll be the technical owner for Quantum; looping in Lena (lena.t@quantumretail.com) who will own infra and certs.
2) Infra constraints: we run behind an API gateway that requires mTLS for upstreams; we also terminate TLS at the gateway so we'd prefer Redwood to connect using a mutual-TLS client cert pair issued by our PKI.
3) Streaming: we definitely want streaming for real-time UX, but we have a hard requirement that any long-lived connections be refreshable and observable by our gateway (idle timeout 10m).
4) Test data: we'll share a seeded test set (CSV with product IDs + user signals) to an S3 bucket with restricted access — I'll share a presigned link.

Acceptance criteria: largely good, but can we relax the cost target slightly for the POC to $0.02 / 1k tokens given model choice? We want to avoid model workarounds during evaluation.

I'll post Lena’s technical requirements separately (she asked to review the checklist first).

—Samir
Samir Patel
Sr. Eng Manager, Quantum Retail
samir@quantumretail.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@quantumretail.com>, Lena Torres <lena.t@quantumretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quantum Retail — POC recap & immediate next steps (integration playbook & routes)

Thanks Samir — understood on mTLS and the gateway idle timeout. Ben and I sketched an integration playbook based on those constraints. Main points below; attaching a short workplan spreadsheet.

Recommended integration approach:
- Primary routes: /v1/stream/chat for streaming-context + function/tool calling (tool calling for product catalog lookups), /v1/generate for batch scoring runs.
- SDK: we recommend starting with our official JS SDK (node) for the frontend proxy; Ben will hand over a snippet that does mTLS over a proxied connection.
- Connection model: short-lived streaming sessions that include reconnection logic and heartbeat pings to satisfy the 10m idle policy. We'll set heartbeat every 5 minutes.
- Prefix caching: enable per-session prefix caching to reduce token costs for repeat requests; we will show tradeoffs in week-2 evaluation runs.

Security / ops notes:
- mTLS: we can support client certs. We will need the public certs and the CA chain to validate on our side; Quantum will need to install the client cert pair into your gateway for redwood endpoints.
- Audit logs: Redwood can retain per-request metadata for the POC window (configurable retention).

Proposed timeline (refined):
- Wed (Week 0 + 3 days): exchange certs + presigned S3 link for test set
- Mon (Week 1): dev kickoff (Ben runs SDK handoff and sample streaming route)
- Week 2–3: integration + nightly profiling/data collection
- Week 4: joint acceptance run and tweak thresholds
- Week 5: findings + handoff notes

Attachments: integration_workplan_v1.xlsx

Ben — I bumped Karthik in to help coordinate quantization/throughput guidance if we need model variants during the POC.

Samir / Lena — could you confirm by EOD whether Quantum can issue a client cert for us to test with? If yes we'll prepare the sample code and an initial test harness.

Best,
Aisha

[Attachment: integration_workplan_v1.xlsx]

From: Lena Torres <lena.t@quantumretail.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@quantumretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:35:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Quantum Retail — POC recap & immediate next steps (integration playbook & routes)

Aisha / Samir — quick technical addendum from infra: 

1) mTLS flow: we can issue a short-lived client cert for Redwood test endpoints. Our security team requires that test certs be rotated weekly and that Redwood present the full cert chain in the TLS handshake.
2) Gateway timeouts: we can extend idle timeout to 12 minutes for test endpoints if heartbeat present.
3) Network: we run Egress through a fixed set of IPs; I'll provide an allowlist for Redwood.

Requests from our engineering team: 
- Can Redwood provide a minimal curl + node SDK example that shows (a) mTLS connection, (b) a streaming response with a function/tool call to a product-catalog endpoint, and (c) reconnection handling?
- Please document headers required for our gateway (we need a consistent x-q-tenant header for attribution).

Acceptance criteria tweak: we'll keep the relevance threshold but set the initial acceptance at top-3 CTR >= 32% for the POC window, with a goal of 35% for production.

I'll attach the infra constraints doc. Once we have the sample code and a presigned S3 link for the test set, we can schedule the dev kickoff.

Thanks,
Lena Torres
Principal Infra Engineer, Quantum Retail
lena.t@quantumretail.com

[Attachment: quantum_api_constraints.docx]
